exactness_definition: STORE-SCOPED: downdate(delete rows) equals the store fitted from scratch without those rows, same partition, same rank. THE FROZEN ENCODER AND DECODER ARE NOT REFIT.

shape_report.caveat: gen_value_holdout.py:299 rejected sphere as a HELD-OUT value because 'a degraded render is a rounded blob, so the SPHERE is the shape the model degrades TOWARDS'. A degrading arm can therefore be judged sphere for rendering reasons rather than store reasons, and would score spuriously well on the deleted conjunction. judged_sphere_excess = frac(judged shape == sphere) - frac(requested shape == sphere); the degraded controls bound how large the artefact can get.

sphere_caveat.HEAD_RULING: the conjunction pin STAYS object_hue = 0.0 AND shape = 2.0 -- the RED SPHERE -- and this caveat column is printed with it
sphere_caveat.verbatim: the shape hazard of section 3.1, exactly: a degraded render is a rounded blob, so the SPHERE is the shape the model degrades TOWARDS. A held-out sphere would be unremovable for rendering reasons, not store reasons
sphere_caveat.what_it_threatens: an arm DAMAGED by the red-sphere deletion could be judged sphere for rendering reasons and score spuriously well on exactly the deleted conjunction

value.scope_definition: every fit row carrying red (object_hue index 0)

our_cost_line.what_happened: post-deletion adaptation is LIGHT and DATA-FREE: the covariance and count are downdated by subtraction, the atoms are re-eigendecomposed from the downdated statistic, and the address book is carried across the basis change. NO ROW OF DATA IS READ.
our_cost_line.the_comparator_pays: a learned baseline can only delete by retraining from scratch WITHOUT the deleted rows -- its cost line is its own and is printed beside this one

receipt.mechanism: S_k -= x x^T, t_k -= x, n_k -= 1; the atoms are re-derived from the statistic and the address book is carried across the basis change by W_k <- W_k R_k, R_k = U_k^T U'_k. The pool is never touched.

basis_change_audit.what: singular values of R_k = U_k^T U'_k are the principal-angle cosines between the pre- and post-deletion spans: 1 where the deletion changed nothing, small where it changed the content. A spectrum that is ALL ones would mean the deletion did nothing.
basis_change_audit.compare_against: the same statistic under a SIZE-MATCHED RANDOM deletion -- if the two agree, the change is generic damage, not targeted forgetting (w5's evict_size_control verdict)

holes.label: red AND cube -- the task file's conjunction
holes.note: shape=cube is held out of the split, so NO red cube was ever written. The hole still makes the request refusable, and that is the point of the row: refusal is a SEPARATE mechanism from forgetting and does not need a deleted row to have existed.

holes.label: red sphere -- the non-vacuous substitute
holes.note: here rows WERE deleted, so the hole and the downdate are exercised on the same conjunction and the two mechanisms are separable on one object

cost_line.note: one byte per hole, two holes

display_refusal.comparator: the refuse-token transformer from spoke/deletion-baselines is the ONLY permitted comparator for a refusal DISPLAY row; the baselines' quantity is their RENDER RATE on the deleted request, not a refusal
display_refusal.comparator_status: DECLARED NOT-RUN here -- see LOG.md for the gate state
display_refusal.carried_caveat: wave 9's refuser separated possible from impossible at only +0.047 and a ridge probe on the same observation scored AUC 0.48-0.55, i.e. chance, so a DISPLAY comparison against a refuser of that quality is not yet informative
display_refusal.what_this_row_is_for: A compositional store can still compose 'red cube' from 'red' and 'cube' after the red-cube rows are gone. THAT IS COMPOSITION WORKING, NOT DELETION FAILING. The hole is the separate mechanism that makes the request refusable, and the two are reported separately on the same object.
